correctness.rationale: Neither g polynomial has a rational root (only ±1 are possible); both are cubic and the displayed roots lie in (3,4) and (12,13). Squaring their roots twice sends (C,D) to (−6,9) to (18,93) and to (−25,167) to (291,27939), respectively, via (C,D)→(C²−2D,D²−2C). These are exactly the coefficients of the minimal polynomials for eta; the defining cubic for theta has negative discriminant and the substitution for eta preserves the unique real root. Thus gamma^4=eta; Q(eta) has degree three and is contained in Q(gamma), so the fields coincide and gamma is a norm-one unit in the full integer ring. Independently, the g discriminants are −135 and −8416. Shifting either polynomial by x=y+1 gives y³−3y−3 and y³−10y²−22y−12. Dedekind's index criterion excludes 3 in the first case and includes 2 in the second; a further factor of 2 in the second index would give a field discriminant ≡2 mod 4, impossible. There are no other candidate primes. The field discriminants are therefore −135 and −2104, agreeing with the frozen index calculations. In rank one a nonfundamental gamma is a proper power of a unit 1<u≤sqrt(gamma); the cited Artin bound would give |D_K|<56 or <232, contradictory. The rank-one regulator is log gamma as stated. Read the frozen notes, verify.py and its recorded verification_output.txt without executing the uploaded code.
